quotes.text: So R-back says, "Mirko can create storage accounts." And Azure Policy says, "Storage accounts must have HTTPS enabled." Two different things and you need both.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes the difference between RBAC and Azure Policy instantly clear.

quotes.text: Azure Policy is always on and it's always enforced. Every single request to create, update or delete a resource passes through Azure Policy and there is no way to bypass it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why policy enforcement is reliable regardless of deployment tool.

quotes.text: Here's the best practice. Start with audit. See what's actually happening in your environment first. Find out how many resources would be affected by a new rule. Then move to deny.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Actionable rollout advice that avoids breaking legitimate deployments.

quotes.text: So even if you've never created a policy yourself, you've probably been using them without knowing it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shows that Azure Policy already powers services like Defender for Cloud and Azure Advisor.

quotes.text: Once you set up Azure Policy properly, it runs silently in the background. It's the automatic guardrail that prevents problems before they happen.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the value of policy as a preventive guardrail.

chapters.title: What Azure Policy is: the invisible rulebook
Effects: deny, audit, modify, deploy if not exists
The big picture of Azure governance

takeaways: Azure Policy controls which resource configurations are allowed, while RBAC controls who may act, and you need both.
Policies are JSON if-then definitions with parameters, assigned at management group, subscription or resource group scope and inherited downward, with exemptions for edge cases.
Start new rules in audit mode, move to deny once you are confident, and bundle related policies into initiatives for a single compliance view.
hook: In the cloud nobody checks your work before a resource is created, so mistakes like public storage or expensive VMs slip through. This episode explains Azure Policy in plain English for anyone responsible for an Azure environment. You learn how definitions, assignments, effects and initiatives enforce your rules automatically on every deployment.
